bc_northeastern_crags.blurb: Northeastern Crags is a group of walls within Skaha Bluffs, the climbing hillside above Skaha Lake just south of Penticton in the Okanagan, British Columbia. Sport routes make up most of the climbing, with a good number of trad lines, and grades cluster between 5.10 and 5.11 with some 5.9s and a smaller set of 5.12s. Skaha's rock is mainly coarse-grained gneiss, with cliffs generally under 30 metres. Morning Glory is sunlit in the morning and shaded soon after midday, while Claim-it-All faces west and is shady in the afternoon. The Euphorium and Far Side also hold a good number of climbs.

ca_east_side_bouldering.blurb: East Side Bouldering is the eastern section of the Holcomb Valley boulders in the San Bernardino Mountains, near Big Bear Lake, California. It is almost entirely bouldering, spread over many separate boulders and small clusters such as the Free Beer Area and The End of the Road, which sit close together. The rock is granite with featured, good-quality surfaces. The selection is moderate: grades run from the very easiest problems to V5, with most between V-easy and V2 and only a few above V3. Across Holcomb Valley the boulders are scattered through forest, and plenty of rock is still unclimbed.

ca_perris_area.blurb: Perris Area gathers the climbing around the city of Perris in California's Inland Empire, from the Big Rock Area at Lake Perris to Juniper Flats and Moreno Valley. Trad leading is the largest piece, alongside a good number of boulder problems and a smaller share of sport and top-rope routes. Roped grades run from 5.4 to 5.12, mostly 5.7 to 5.11, and boulders go from V0 to V6. At Big Rock the rock is a granite monolith about 180 feet tall, with mostly single-pitch or top-rope climbs that suit beginner and intermediate climbers. It is open year round, with the best conditions from late September to mid-June, and the west face is shaded in the morning.

ca_placerville.blurb: Placerville climbing lies around the town where Highways 50 and 49 cross, in the Sierra foothills on the Lake Tahoe side of California. It has two sub-areas, Cosumnes River Gorge and Mosquito Coast. Trad and top-rope climbing lead, with a good number of boulder problems and a few sport routes. Roped grades run from 5.6 to 5.12 and cluster between 5.8 and 5.10. At the gorge the rock is granite and the river runs through the canyon; Bucks Bar Dome is the main area for top-roping, and Gutenberger Wall across the river has multipitch trad. Summer at the gorge is very hot, so mornings or late afternoons are better.

ca_virgin_islands_area.blurb: Virgin Islands Area is a cluster of rock formations off Geology Tour Road in the Queen Valley part of Joshua Tree National Park. Bouldering and trad cracks share the stage, with a smaller amount of sport and a few top-rope lines. Boulder problems run from the easiest grades to V8 but mostly sit at the low end, while roped climbs span 5.8 to 5.12 and cluster around 5.10 and 5.11. The area is known for crack and face climbing. Star Wars Rock is a large formation with crack routes on its west face and an overhanging south face. Other spots include the Volcano Area, Perpetual Motion Wall and Lechlinski Crack Formation.

co_fern_canyon.blurb: Fern Canyon is a minor gully in the southern Flatirons, on the northeast side of Bear Peak near Boulder, Colorado. Trad climbing leads, with a good number of boulder problems and a smaller group of sport routes. Roped grades run from 5.2 to 5.13, mostly 5.8 to 5.12, and boulders from V1 to V9. Most routes are short, one or two pitches, and mostly face climbs. Many face south, which makes them good for sunny fall and winter days. Nebel Horn Ridge is a stepped formation with trad, sport and top-rope lines, and Fiddlehead and East Ridge are other main crags, with Fern Canyon Bouldering holding the boulders.
